claims.text: On this trip's own figures the excess is 4.0 km and 36.36% over the 11.0 km routing-engine optimal stored on the trip record, so both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates are met (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), and the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km at 15.0 km rather than the rounded trip_record convenience copy. I disclose that the trace this rests on is IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP; the policy consequence of that impairment is set out in the following claims.

The trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely by the schema pre-pass: the single 160-second gap at 20:03:10-20:05:50 exceeds POL-RD-07(a)'s 90-second limit, and the 1.35 km straight-line jump across that gap exceeds POL-RD-07(b)'s 500 m limit, so the artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP; under POL-GEN-02(2) any finding carried solely by this artifact is capped at 0.6, below the 0.70 platform escalation floor.

No POL-RD-07(ii) independent source exists on this record: the chat log carries no driver admission of a detour (the driver reports only that his navigation display refreshed and he continued), the fare_breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, the driver's counterparty_statement denies the detour rather than admitting the route, and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km (15.0 km) is a copy of the trace figure rather than an independent derivation. POL-RD-07(iii) therefore applies and the outcome is ESCALATE under POL-RD-10(3), which holds the disputed SGD 5.80 rather than collecting it.

The driver has no exculpatory clause to invoke: the only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09115-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no advisory covers this road or trip window and POL-RD-03 cannot run; trip_record.pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null and name no road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and that clause is unavailable; and vehicle_type RYDE_X is not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is not aggravated: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition for unsubstantiated repeat claimants is not triggered, and the artifacts describe the same trip with a matching identifier, TRP-09115, across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown.

Should the deviation be sustained notwithstanding the impairment, POL-RD-02 runs because fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.0 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.1, the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.831; refund = charged_total 26.60 - 20.831 = 5.769, rounded UP to SGD 5.80, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is the precise amount the rider contests.

claims.text: The trace the rider relies on is impaired on the very segment he disputes. EV-GPS-09115 carries a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes (20:03:10 to 20:05:50, with a 1.35 km straight-line jump across it), which is well over the 90-second threshold in POL-RD-07 limb (a), and the admissibility pre-pass tags the artifact IMPAIRED with issue code GPS_GAP at weight 0.6. I disclose that impairment and those issue codes: the trace is impaired for policy purposes, so a deviation cannot be established on it alone.

Under POL-RD-07 limb (i) the distance across that impaired stretch is measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes, which is the reading most favourable to the driver, and on this record that is 1.35 km. The rider's own claim places the departure from the booked route at the gap itself, so the stretch the policy deems unreliable is exactly the stretch from which his 4 km excess is drawn. (Evidence cited is impaired: EV-GPS-09115, issue GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

The excess has no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07 limb (ii) demands. The pool contains only three distance figures — gps_trace.trace_distance_km 15.0, trip_record.actual_distance_km 15.0 and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km 15.0 — and they are one and the same measurement: POL-RD-01 describes actual_distance_km as a rounded convenience copy of the trace measurement, and POL-RD-07 limb (ii) expressly excludes a billed distance that is a copy of the trace figure. Not one of them is independent. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

Nor does any other limb (ii) source exist. The fare_breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The chat log records only the rider reporting that the route display jumped and the driver answering that his own navigation display refreshed — a report of a display glitch, not an admission of a detour. The driver's counterparty statement denies any extra stop or detour request and candidly states that he cannot account for the telemetry gap. That is a denial, not the admission the clause requires.

Because the impaired trace stands uncorroborated, POL-RD-07 limb (iii) directs that the claim is not sustained on the present record and that the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION — the absence of proof here is a data failure, not a finding for the driver. The rider's asserted 4 km excess therefore cannot be converted into a refund on this evidence. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

Escalation is in any event mandatory under POL-RD-10 limb (3): the gps_trace is impaired under POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07 limb (ii) names exists in the pool. Independently, the fact that decides this case — the impairment itself — is carried only by an artifact at weight 0.6, so confidence is capped at 0.6 under POL-GEN-02 and sits below the platform-wide 0.70 floor that POL-RD-10 limb (1) applies. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The trip identifiers do match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so element (a) is satisfied; but element (b) requires an excess measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07 limb (ii). The trace is impaired and no independent source exists, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the prima facie case fails. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

Even taken at face value, this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The 36.4% and 4.0 km excess clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate but falls short of the 50% and 8.0 km materiality tests, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged on materiality. No pattern exists in any event: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 610 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, so neither the limb (b) uplift nor the limb (c) conduct referral is available against this driver.

The disposition the record supports is ESCALATE, and on this rider-filed dispute that outcome preserves the driver's position: escalation holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it, and does not restore or issue any refund to the rider. Nothing is returned to the rider and the fare stands pending human review. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

ruling.explanation:
This ruling concerns trip TRP-09115 (Upper Thomson Grove to Yio Chu Kang South community hall, 22 September 2026) and the SGD 5.80 the rider contests.

The trip's GPS trace (EV-GPS-09115) has a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes (20:03:10 to 20:05:50) with a 1.35 km straight-line jump across it. Both figures exceed the limits in POL-RD-07(a) and (b) (90 seconds; 500 m), so the trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely flagged by the pre-pass. It carries admissibility weight 0.6 and issue code GPS_GAP, and I name both as POL-GEN-02(3) requires.

The rider's 4.0 km / 36.4% excess is drawn entirely from that trace. POL-RD-07(ii) says a deviation may not be established on an impaired trace alone; it needs corroboration from one of four independent sources, and none is present:
- The chat log (EV-CHAT-09115) records only the rider's report that the route display jumped and the driver's reply that his own navigation display refreshed; neither is an admission of a detour, and no road or waypoint is named (both waypoint_hint fields are null).
- The fare breakdown's ERP gantry list is empty, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use.
- The driver's statement denies any extra stop or detour request; a denial is not the admission the clause requires.
- The three distance figures (gps_trace.trace_distance_km 15.0, trip_record.actual_distance_km 15.0, fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km 15.0) are one and the same measurement — POL-RD-01 describes the trip-record figure as a rounded convenience copy of the trace — so none is an independent source.

Because the impaired trace stands uncorroborated, POL-RD-07(iii) directs that the claim is not sustained on the present record and that the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION: the absence of proof is a data failure, not a finding for the driver. POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory. Separately, the impairment fact is carried only by an artifact at weight 0.6, so my confidence is capped at 0.6 under POL-GEN-02(2) — below the 0.70 floor — which independently triggers POL-RD-10(1).

On the rider's POL-RD-01 point: the numbers (4.0 km and 36.4% over the 11.0 km routing-engine optimal) do clear the 0.8 km and 20% establishment gates on the trace, but the trace is impaired, so the gate cannot be passed on the trace alone. The rider's POL-RD-02 arithmetic (charged 26.60; recomputed fare 20.831 using the fare_breakdown surge multiplier of 1.1; refund 5.77 rounded up to 5.80) is correct as far as it goes but is not reached, because the deviation it depends on is not established. The driver likewise has no exculpatory clause to invoke — the only traffic advisory is MISSING at weight 0.0, there is no pickup or dropoff amendment, no waypoint is resolved, and the vehicle type RYDE_X is not a pool — but that does not matter, because the rider's case cannot be proved on this record. The deviation is not MATERIAL (36.4% < 50%, 4.0 km < 8.0 km) and the driver shows no trailing-90-day pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 610 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises; and every fare line is matched (erp_gantries empty, no airport surcharge), so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises.

What the human reviewer needs to resolve this is a distance figure for the unobserved segment that does not depend on the broken trace — a platform-derived actual distance, a gantry record placing the vehicle off the booked corridor, or an admission — or a trace without the gap. Escalation is terminal: nothing is collected and nothing is refunded, and the disputed SGD 5.80 is held pending that review.

Both parties: the disputed SGD 5.80 is held, not refunded and not confirmed, and the case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves today, and the fare stands pending that review.

WHY. The governing GPS trace for this trip (EV-GPS-09115) is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It contains a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes, from 20:03:10 to 20:05:50, which is over the 90-second limit in POL-RD-07(a), and a 1.35 km straight-line jump across that gap, which is over the 500 m limit in POL-RD-07(b). The admissibility pre-pass independently tagged the artifact IMPAIRED with issue code GPS_GAP at weight 0.6, and I record both things out loud: schema-IMPAIRED and policy-IMPAIRED. The gap sits on the very stretch the rider says the vehicle left the booked road, so the point where the route-shape evidence is missing is the point the claim turns on.

CONSEQUENCE. Because the trace is impaired, POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing a deviation on the trace alone; it must be corroborated by an independent source — a driver admission in the chat log, charged ERP gantries putting the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, a counterparty statement admitting the route, or a trip distance the platform derived independently of this trace. None exists. The chat log (EV-CHAT-09115) records only the rider reporting that the route display jumped and the driver replying that his own navigation refreshed and he continued — a display-glitch report, not a detour admission. The driver's statement denies any extra stop or detour request and candidly says he cannot account for the telemetry gap; that is a denial, not the admission the clause requires. The fare breakdown's erp_gantries list is empty, so no charged gantry places the vehicle off-corridor. And the trip_record and fare breakdown distances (15.0 km) are not independent of the trace: POL-RD-01 describes actual_distance_km as a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement, and the meter is derived from the same trace, so all three 15.0 km figures are one measurement, not three. POL-RD-07(iii) therefore applies: on this record the claim is neither proven nor disproven, and the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because the missing proof is a data failure and not a finding for the driver.

This is also mandatory escalation under POL-RD-10(3), and separately under POL-RD-10(1): the fact that decides the case is carried only by EV-GPS-09115 at weight 0.6, so confidence is capped at 0.6 under POL-GEN-02(2), below the 0.70 platform floor that clause applies. The rider's POL-RD-08 initial burden likewise fails at element (b), because the trace is impaired and no POL-RD-07(ii) source stands in for it.

ON THE SURVIVING CLAIMS. The rider's POL-RD-01 arithmetic is accepted — 4.0 km and 36.36% over the 11.0 km routing-engine optimal clears both establishment gates, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km (15.0 km) is rightly used as the governing figure — but it does not decide the case, because a deviation cannot be established on this impaired, uncorroborated trace. The rider's POL-RD-02 computation is correct as arithmetic (charged_total 26.60, recomputed_fare 20.831, refund 5.769 rounded up to 5.80) but it does not run: POL-RD-02 operates only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and here it is not. No refund of the 5.80 is ordered.

The driver's points are accepted. No exculpatory clause is available: the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09115-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot run; neither endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run because both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null and name no road, so that clause is unavailable; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The excess, though established on paper, is not MATERIAL (it is under 50% and under 8.0 km), and no POL-RD-06 pattern exists on the citable counters (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 610 completed trips in the trailing 90 days), so no driver-conduct referral and no FULL_REFUND uplift arise. No charge line is unmatched, so POL-RD-10(8) does not fire, and with erp_gantries empty and no airport surcharge there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral. The referrals list is therefore empty.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT. A corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names — a driver admission in the chat log, a charged ERP gantry on an off-optimal corridor, a counterparty statement admitting the route, or an independently derived trip distance — or a continuous, repaired GPS trace covering 20:03:10 to 20:05:50. The reviewer is asked to obtain one of those before the disputed amount is settled either way.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the GPS trace that would decide this case is broken over the very stretch in dispute, and nothing independent repairs it, so the case must go to a human reviewer. No money moves now: the disputed SGD 5.80 is held rather than collected or refunded.

THE IMPAIRED TRACE. Both sides agree, and I find, that EV-GPS-09115 is impaired. It carries a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes (20:03:10 to 20:05:50) with a 1.35 km straight-line jump across it. I say both things the policy requires: the artifact is IMPAIRED at the schema level (the admissibility pre-pass tags it GPS_GAP and down-weights it to 0.6), and it is independently IMPAIRED for policy purposes, because the gap exceeds POL-RD-07(a)'s 90-second limit and the jump exceeds POL-RD-07(b)'s 500 m limit.

WHY THIS ESCALATES. The rider's own account places the departure from the booked road at the gap, so the stretch the policy deems unreliable is exactly the stretch the claimed 4.0 km excess is drawn from. Under POL-RD-07(ii) a deviation cannot be established on an impaired trace alone; it needs a source independent of the trace. There is none. The chat log records only a display glitch (the rider's report that the route display jumped, the driver's answer that his navigation display also refreshed) and no driver admission of a detour. The fare_breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty, so no charged gantry places the vehicle off the optimal corridor. The driver's counterparty_statement denies any extra stop or detour request and does not admit the route. And the three distance figures in the pool (gps_trace.trace_distance_km 15.0, trip_record.actual_distance_km 15.0, fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km 15.0) are one and the same measurement: POL-RD-01 describes actual_distance_km as a rounded convenience copy of the trace figure, and POL-RD-07(ii) expressly excludes a billed distance that copies the trace. Because the impaired trace stands uncorroborated, POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) direct ESCALATE rather than a finding for either side - a data gap is a failure of proof, not a finding that the driver did nothing wrong. Independently, the only fact that could decide this case is carried by EV-GPS-09115 at weight 0.6, so confidence is capped at 0.6 under POL-GEN-02(2), below the platform-wide 0.70 floor that POL-RD-10(1) applies. ESCALATE is terminal and replaces any money ruling here.

THE RIDER'S CLAIMS. The arithmetic is correct: 4.0 km and 36.4% over the 11.0 km routing-engine optimal stored on the trip record clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km), and had the trace been sound the POL-RD-02 recomputation - charged_total 26.60, recomputed_fare 20.831 using the fare_breakdown surge_multiplier of 1.1, refund 5.769 rounded up to 5.80 - would have been payable. But the establishment cannot be made on an impaired, uncorroborated trace, so that refund does not issue on this record. The rider is also right that no exculpatory clause runs for the driver: EV-ADVIS-09115-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) so POL-RD-03 cannot run; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null so POL-RD-05 cannot run; both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null and name no road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; and vehicle_type RYDE_X is not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. That removes any exoneration but does not supply the independent corroboration the rider needs.

THE DRIVER'S CLAIMS. I accept that the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(b); that the impaired stretch reads as the 1.35 km straight line between bounding fixes, the reading most favourable to the driver; that no POL-RD-07(ii) source exists; and that under POL-RD-08 the rider's initial burden is not discharged, so it never shifts. I also accept that this is not a MATERIAL deviation - 36.4% and 4.0 km fall short of the 50% and 8.0 km tests - and that no POL-RD-06 pattern exists (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 610 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, the only fields that clause permits), so there is no conduct referral and no remedy uplift against this driver. Escalation preserves the fare pending review; it is not a ruling in the driver's favour, and it refunds nothing to the rider.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT. A source of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names - a driver admission in the chat log, charged ERP gantries placing the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, a counterparty statement admitting the route, or a trip_record.actual_distance_km the platform derived independently of this trace - or a repaired trace covering 20:03 to 20:06. None is in the present record.

discards.claim: No POL-RD-07(ii) independent source exists on this record: the chat log carries no driver admission of a detour (the driver reports only that his navigation display refreshed and he continued), the fare_breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, the driver's counterparty_statement denies the detour rather than admitting the route, and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km (15.0 km) is a copy of the trace figure rather than an independent derivation. POL-RD-07(iii) therefore applies and the outcome is ESCALATE under POL-RD-10(3), which holds the disputed SGD 5.80 rather than collecting it.

ledger.claim: On this trip's own figures the excess is 4.0 km and 36.36% over the 11.0 km routing-engine optimal stored on the trip record, so both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates are met (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), and the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km at 15.0 km rather than the rounded trip_record convenience copy. I disclose that the trace this rests on is IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP; the policy consequence of that impairment is set out in the following claims.

The trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely by the schema pre-pass: the single 160-second gap at 20:03:10-20:05:50 exceeds POL-RD-07(a)'s 90-second limit, and the 1.35 km straight-line jump across that gap exceeds POL-RD-07(b)'s 500 m limit, so the artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP; under POL-GEN-02(2) any finding carried solely by this artifact is capped at 0.6, below the 0.70 platform escalation floor.

No POL-RD-07(ii) independent source exists on this record: the chat log carries no driver admission of a detour (the driver reports only that his navigation display refreshed and he continued), the fare_breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, the driver's counterparty_statement denies the detour rather than admitting the route, and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km (15.0 km) is a copy of the trace figure rather than an independent derivation. POL-RD-07(iii) therefore applies and the outcome is ESCALATE under POL-RD-10(3), which holds the disputed SGD 5.80 rather than collecting it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is not aggravated: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the extra-corroboration condition for unsubstantiated repeat claimants is not triggered, and the artifacts describe the same trip with a matching identifier, TRP-09115, across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown.

ledger.claim: Should the deviation be sustained notwithstanding the impairment, POL-RD-02 runs because fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.0 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.1, the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.831; refund = charged_total 26.60 - 20.831 = 5.769, rounded UP to SGD 5.80, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is the precise amount the rider contests.

The trace the rider relies on is impaired on the very segment he disputes. EV-GPS-09115 carries a 160-second gap between consecutive fixes (20:03:10 to 20:05:50, with a 1.35 km straight-line jump across it), which is well over the 90-second threshold in POL-RD-07 limb (a), and the admissibility pre-pass tags the artifact IMPAIRED with issue code GPS_GAP at weight 0.6. I disclose that impairment and those issue codes: the trace is impaired for policy purposes, so a deviation cannot be established on it alone.

Under POL-RD-07 limb (i) the distance across that impaired stretch is measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes, which is the reading most favourable to the driver, and on this record that is 1.35 km. The rider's own claim places the departure from the booked route at the gap itself, so the stretch the policy deems unreliable is exactly the stretch from which his 4 km excess is drawn. (Evidence cited is impaired: EV-GPS-09115, issue GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

The excess has no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07 limb (ii) demands. The pool contains only three distance figures — gps_trace.trace_distance_km 15.0, trip_record.actual_distance_km 15.0 and fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km 15.0 — and they are one and the same measurement: POL-RD-01 describes actual_distance_km as a rounded convenience copy of the trace measurement, and POL-RD-07 limb (ii) expressly excludes a billed distance that is a copy of the trace figure. Not one of them is independent. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

Nor does any other limb (ii) source exist. The fare_breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The chat log records only the rider reporting that the route display jumped and the driver answering that his own navigation display refreshed — a report of a display glitch, not an admission of a detour. The driver's counterparty statement denies any extra stop or detour request and candidly states that he cannot account for the telemetry gap. That is a denial, not the admission the clause requires.

Because the impaired trace stands uncorroborated, POL-RD-07 limb (iii) directs that the claim is not sustained on the present record and that the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION — the absence of proof here is a data failure, not a finding for the driver. The rider's asserted 4 km excess therefore cannot be converted into a refund on this evidence. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

Escalation is in any event mandatory under POL-RD-10 limb (3): the gps_trace is impaired under POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07 limb (ii) names exists in the pool. Independently, the fact that decides this case — the impairment itself — is carried only by an artifact at weight 0.6, so confidence is capped at 0.6 under POL-GEN-02 and sits below the platform-wide 0.70 floor that POL-RD-10 limb (1) applies. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The trip identifiers do match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so element (a) is satisfied; but element (b) requires an excess measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07 limb (ii). The trace is impaired and no independent source exists, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the prima facie case fails. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)

Even taken at face value, this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The 36.4% and 4.0 km excess clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate but falls short of the 50% and 8.0 km materiality tests, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged on materiality. No pattern exists in any event: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 610 completed trips in the trailing 90 days, so neither the limb (b) uplift nor the limb (c) conduct referral is available against this driver.

The disposition the record supports is ESCALATE, and on this rider-filed dispute that outcome preserves the driver's position: escalation holds the disputed amount rather than collecting or refunding it, and does not restore or issue any refund to the rider. Nothing is returned to the rider and the fare stands pending human review. (EV-GPS-09115 is impaired: GPS_GAP, weight 0.6.)
